title: Devin Integration: How to Set It Up (2026 Guide)
summary: Devin integration connects to task sources like Slack, GitHub, and ticket tools. You'll decide how narrowly to limit the permissions it receives.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Once you compare review minutes against work saved, a few narrow questions are left, and each has a short answer.


Does Devin integrate with Jira and Linear? Yes, both are supported as places where a task can start, alongside Slack. Connect one project or team first, not the whole workspace.


If a ticket can trigger a session, then everyone who can file or label a ticket can spend your usage, so decide who that's before you switch it on.


Can I use Devin without connecting GitHub? Yes, if your code lives on another supported host, since GitHub's one of several source integrations.


Without any repository connection, Devin can still work in a session, but it has nothing to open a pull request against. That makes the output harder to review, so the review minutes you measured earlier will likely go up.


Does Devin have a public API? Yes. It lets you create and monitor sessions from your own systems, which is the cleanest way to start work from a trigger you control instead of a chat message.


Issue a dedicated credential for each use, so that when one misbehaves you can revoke it without breaking the others.


### Can Devin work in a private repository?


Yes. Grant access to the specific repositories it needs, not the whole organization. Write access is needed only if you want Devin to push branches and open pull requests.


Pair that with branch protection and required human review on the main branch, so a session can propose a change but never merge one.


If a session runs away, that is a separate matter from permissions. Terminate it from the session view, then revoke the credential behind the integration that started it. Stopping the session ends the spend, while revoking the credential prevents the same trigger from starting another.


Is Devin integration included in every plan? Not necessarily. Which integrations and API features you get depends on your plan, and vendors change those tiers often.


Check the current pricing page against the exact triggers you intend to use before you commit. If a trigger you need sits on a higher tier, count that cost against the work saved, the same way you counted review minutes.
